about: Verdicts on single games. "no-stutter": the game prepares its shaders itself, so SCSKiller doesn't suggest compiling it but still allows it. "unsupported-yet" and "unsupported": never compiled, recorded or queued. "no-anti-cheat": a WeGame game confirmed clean, the only way one gets a recorder. "anti-cheat": the game counts as one with anti-cheat, also by the whole file names in exes, and this only adds to the app's own lists. reason is a code the app words itself: engine-precompiles, driver-cache-ignored, anti-cheat, crashes, engine-unreadable, or other with a note. An unknown code shows the note. ids are Game.Id values. engines ("Unreal 5.7" takes 5.7.x) and builds (store build ids) limit an entry. source is never shown but this file is public. date = when the entry was last checked. This is the body: the server serves it signed (release-sign sign-content --name game-verdicts). The app skips an entry it can't read, so later versions can add members, verdicts and codes.
